2607.24056.title: Capacity-Aware Deep Learning for Generalizable Traffic Volume Estimation Across Links and Cities
2607.24056.paper_summary: Network-wide traffic volume estimation typically relies on propagating measurements from fixed sensors, making performance highly dependent on sensor density and limiting deployment in sparsely instrumented networks. We propose a link-level learning framework that estimates hourly traffic volumes from widely available territorial data only, including probe speed profiles, road and topological descriptors, along with weather observations. A supervised local mapping is learned from sparse sensor measurements and evaluated under two generalization settings: intra-network (unseen links within the training network) and inter-network (unseen city). This formulation frames traffic volume estimation as a spatial out-of-distribution generalization problem under sparse supervision. To enhance spatial robustness, we introduce a capacity-aware formulation that models volume as the product of a link-specific structural capacity and an hourly regime-aware utilization ratio, embedding traffic-theoretic constraints directly into the learning process. Extensive experiments in both generalization settings demonstrate that the proposed structural constraints consistently outperform a state-of-the-art baseline under spatial distribution shift.
2607.24056.paper_summary_zh: 網絡範圍內的流量估算通常依賴於從固定傳感器傳播的測量，這使得性能高度依賴於傳感器的密度，並限制了在儀器稀疏的網絡中的部署。我們提出了一個鏈路級學習框架，僅通過廣泛可用的地區數據來估算每小時的流量，包括探測速度曲線、道路和拓撲描述符，以及天氣觀測。從稀疏的傳感器測量中學習一個監督的局部映射，並在兩種泛化設置下進行評估：網內（訓練網絡內的未見鏈路）和網間（未見城市）。這一公式將流量估算框架化為一個在稀疏監督下的空間分佈外泛化問題。為了增強空間穩健性，我們引入了一個考慮容量的公式，將流量建模為鏈路特定結構容量與每小時狀態感知利用率的乘積，將交通理論約束直接嵌入學習過程中。在兩種泛化設置下的廣泛實驗表明，所提出的結構約束在空間分佈轉變下始終優於最先進的基準。
